messages.content: What is the current temperature and humidity in New York, Los Angeles, London and Tokyo, if I want to include both temperature and humidity in the results?

function.name: get_current_weather
function.description: Retrieves the current temperature and humidity for a specific location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to get the weather for.

include_temperature.description: Whether to include the temperature in the result. Default is true.

include_humidity.description: Whether to include the humidity in the result. Default is true.

message.reasoning:
The user wants current temperature and humidity for four cities: New York, Los Angeles, London, Tokyo. They want both temperature and humidity. We have a function get_current_weather that can retrieve data for a specific location. It takes location string, include_temperature default true, include_humidity default true. So we need to call this function for each city. But the function signature only accepts one location at a time. We could call it four times. Or maybe we can pass multiple locations? The function signature expects a single location string. So we need to call it four times.

We should call the function with location "New York", include_temperature true, include_humidity true. Then same for Los Angeles, London, Tokyo. The user didn't specify units; we can assume default. We'll call the function four times.
